version: arXiv:1601.08166v1; manuscript dated 2021-07-15 in extracted copy; 15 PDF pages

read_ranges.scope: entire paper: both denominator cases, convergence proofs, KL argument, future-work section and references

topic_relevance.A01: direct: develops proximal-gradient algorithms for positive-denominator fractional minimization and analyzes value/iterate convergence.

definitions.name: fractional program
definitions.statement: θ=inf_{x∈S} f(x)/g(x), with f≥0 on S and g>0 on S.

definitions.name: concave-denominator assumptions
definitions.statement: S is nonempty closed convex; f is proper convex lsc, dom f intersects S and f≥0; g is concave, differentiable with L-Lipschitz gradient and 0<g≤M on S.

definitions.name: KL property
definitions.statement: A desingularizing function ϕ makes ϕ′(h(x)−h(x̄)) dist(0,∂_L h(x))≥1 near the reference value and point.

definitions.name: proximal-gradient iteration
definitions.statement: The iteration combines a proximal minimization for f+δ_S with a gradient step for the denominator.

definitions.name: quotient parameter update
definitions.statement: At each iterate the parameter is updated as θ_{k+1}=f(x_k)/g(x_k).

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 7 (concave denominator)
assumptions: For weak convergence of x_k, inf_{x∈S} f(x)/g(x)>0
theorem_cards.statement: θ_k is nonincreasing and converges to θ; the objective error has an O(1/k) upper bound depending on initial distance and g(x). Under the additional positive lower bound on the optimal ratio, x_k converges weakly to an optimal solution.
proof_steps: Optimality of the proximal step gives a subgradient inequality.
Concavity of g and the descent lemma yield a Lyapunov inequality combining objective gap, step norm and distance to an optimizer.
Summability proves θ_k↓θ and yields the stated rate by telescoping.
When θ>0, step differences vanish and distances to every optimizer converge; Opial’s lemma gives weak convergence.
gaps: The value convergence/rate does not itself ensure iterate convergence; the positive infimum of f/g is separately required. If θ_1=0, the displayed step-size 1/(2Lθ_1) is singular, although x_0 already certifies the optimum because f≥0.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 10 (convex denominator, limit-point stationarity)
assumptions: Problem 8 assumptions: f proper convex lsc and nonnegative; g convex differentiable with L-Lipschitz gradient and 0<g≤M
theorem_cards.statement: θ_k is nonincreasing and Σ||x_k−x_{k−1}||²/η_k<∞. Every strong cluster point x lies in dom f∩S and has limiting ratio θ=f(x)/g(x); if x is in int(dom f∩S), it is a limiting-subdifferential critical point of (f+δ_S)/g.
proof_steps: Proximal optimality plus convexity of g gives a decrease inequality for θ_k and a squared-step bound.
At a strong limit point, lower semicontinuity and continuity of g identify the limiting quotient.
Closedness of the convex subdifferential gives θ∇g(x)∈∂(f+δ_S)(x).
An interior subdifferential quotient rule converts this to 0∈∂_L((f+δ_S)/g)(x).
gaps: No whole-sequence convergence or global optimality is claimed here; for convex g, the limit point may only be critical.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 15 (whole-sequence convergence under KL)
assumptions: liminf η_k>0, η_1θ_1<1/L, and η_k nonincreasing
(x_k) bounded and eventually in int(dom f∩S)
theorem_cards.statement: The sequence has finite length Σ||x_{k+1}−x_k||<∞ and converges to x∞; if x∞ is interior, it is a limiting critical point.
proof_steps: The cluster set is compact and connected and the objective is constant on it by Lemma 13.
Uniformized KL inequality controls the objective gap by a subgradient residual.
Descent gives a sufficient-decrease inequality and proximal optimality gives a relative-error estimate.
Combine these inequalities to obtain finite path length, then Cauchy convergence.
gaps: The proof relies on the eventual-interiority assumption for the quotient subdifferential rule, boundedness, and uniform η bounds; no general global-optimum conclusion is available.

constant_dependence.explicit: For the concave case η_k=1/(2Lθ_k); the objective estimate is O(1/k) with constants involving θ_1, denominator upper bound M, initial distance ||x−x_0||² and g(x). For the convex case, sufficient decrease depends on η_k, L and θ_k.
constant_dependence.dependence: No dimension-free cube maximal inequality is derived; the convergence results are optimization-algorithm statements in Hilbert spaces.

endpoint_limits.denominator: g must be strictly positive on the feasible set; concave/convex denominator is smooth with Lipschitz gradient and bounded above.
endpoint_limits.concave_case: Weak convergence of iterates additionally needs the optimal ratio bounded away from zero.
endpoint_limits.convex_case: Without the KL and interior assumptions, only objective convergence/cluster-point properties are stated; critical points need not be globally optimal.
endpoint_limits.zero_ratio: If the initial ratio is zero with f≥0, x_0 is already a global optimizer, but the paper does not define the infinite step parameter case; stop at that certificate.

reusable_methods.method: Dinkelbach residual f−θg paired with proximal-gradient splitting
reusable_methods.transfer: A solver pattern for fractional minimization when numerator is convex nonsmooth and denominator is smooth with the stated curvature/sign conditions; it is not a proof of weak-type bounds for the continuous maximal-cube operator.

reusable_methods.method: Separate value convergence from iterate convergence
reusable_methods.transfer: When reporting a numerical ratio algorithm, state whether only θ_k converges, whether weak/strong iterates converge, and which positivity/KL/interiority assumptions support each claim.

reusable_methods.method: Use a Lyapunov inequality plus Opial or KL finite-length argument
reusable_methods.transfer: Reusable proof architecture only after verifying the corresponding Hilbert/finite-dimensional compactness and subdifferential conditions.

unchecked: I read the full paper and checked the ratio-update identity, the sign of the descent inequality, and the distinction between concave-denominator global convergence and convex-denominator criticality. I did not independently reprove the cited Opial, subdifferential calculus, or KL framework results, nor run the algorithms. Those claims rely on the authors’ stated references.
